subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB358 LANDED 2026-09-09. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 'becomes the key of reference' -> OK, GR16): 'The key specified in the KEY phrase, or that shares a leftmost character with the data item specified in the KEY phrase, becomes the key of reference... If the execution of the START statement is successful, this key of reference is used for subsequent sequential READ statements referencing file-name-1.'
WHY CONFORMS RATHER THAN PARTIAL: the same reason recorded on GR-14.9.41.4-15. GR16's subject is the key of reference, a claimed facility; the record-key-name-1 operand spelling rides on the SOURCE phrase, which is Annex A.3 item 40's declined processor-dependent element and is now REFUSED BY NAME (COBOL1954, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40). The declined half is owned and witnessed by SR-14.9.41.3-7.
BOTH IMPLEMENTED ARMS AND THE PERSISTENCE WERE ALREADY MEASURED and are pinned by conformance:cases/14.9.9-CONTINUE/altkey_suppress_when (START KEY >= on the alternate key, then a full READ NEXT walk in alternate order - the named-key arm and the persistence) and conformance:cases/12.4.5.7-COLLATING-SEQUENCE/file_collating_seq (START KEY >= 'M' under a reversed alphabet, then the walk M,A). The leftmost-coincident arm ('or that shares a leftmost character with the data item specified in the KEY phrase') was measured on probe start-p2-d and is resolved by RecordLayout.GenericKeyIndex behind KeyIndexOfKeyItem. IndexedConnector.Start assigns _refKey only AFTER a record is found, so an unsuccessful START leaves it alone (GR7's 'undefined' is part 1/3's row), and ReadSequential walks Ordered(_refKey).
NEW COVERAGE FOR THE OMITTED-KEY-PHRASE CASE: conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb358_start_no_key_phrase leg L1N. GR15 makes the prime record key the key of reference when the KEY phrase is absent, so the READ NEXT after the one that delivered AB02 must deliver CD03 - PRIME order. The records are written AB01, CD03, AB02, deliberately NOT in key order, so a walk that merely followed insertion order would answer AB01 there. Until this golden the persistence sentence was pinned only for an EXPLICIT KEY phrase.
EDITIONS: no edition marker in the clause; Annex E lists no START change. kb/Work PB1099 Q1 (w1095i): the record-key SOURCE phrase is PROVIDED (owner rule R65); START KEY IS > IX-AK makes the SOURCE-form alternate key the key of reference (golden S1-S4). retired-witness: conformance:cases/12.4.5.6-ALTERNATE-RECORD-KEY/pb358-record-key-source (the COBOL1954 decline of the SOURCE phrase is retired: kb/Work PB1099 provides it)
